claims.article_title: The 49-Point Gap: What SWE-bench Science's Visible-Test Scores Hide
claims.claim: Claude Code with Opus-5 (max) is the best-performing agent on SWE-bench Science, achieving a Pass@1 of 47.90% on private tests.

claims.article_title: The 49-Point Gap: What SWE-bench Science's Visible-Test Scores Hide
claims.claim: Claude-Opus-5 records the lowest categorized scientific-error count (58) plus four runtime/evaluation-path failures, and the fewest misguided-exploration errors (2).

claims.article_title: The 49-Point Gap: What SWE-bench Science's Visible-Test Scores Hide
claims.claim: In a paired ablation on a 91-task subset, adding scientific information lowered GPT-5.6-sol's Pass@1 from 36.26% to 31.87% but raised DeepSeek-V4-flash's from 16.48% to 23.08%.

claims.article_title: The 49-Point Gap: What SWE-bench Science's Visible-Test Scores Hide
claims.claim: Scientific information slightly raises GPT-5.6-sol's mean public/private scores (96.70% to 97.80% and 73.23% to 74.06%) while its Pass@1 falls from 36.26% to 31.87%.

claims.article_title: The 49-Point Gap: What SWE-bench Science's Visible-Test Scores Hide
claims.claim: The paper states the paired ablation differences are descriptive and do not establish statistical significance or a causal effect.

claims.article_title: The 49-Point Gap: What SWE-bench Science's Visible-Test Scores Hide
claims.claim: SWE-ABS found 19.78% of 11,041 previously-passing top-30 patches on SWE-bench Verified to be semantically incorrect, cutting the top agent from 78.80% to 62.20%.

claims.article_title: The 49-Point Gap: What SWE-bench Science's Visible-Test Scores Hide
claims.claim: SWE-bench+ attributed 32.67% of successful patches from top systems to solution leakage from issue reports.

claims.article_title: The 49-Point Gap: What SWE-bench Science's Visible-Test Scores Hide
claims.claim: UTBoost identified 345 erroneous patches incorrectly labeled as passed in the original SWE-Bench, affecting 40.9% of SWE-Bench Lite and 24.4% of SWE-Bench Verified leaderboard entries.

claims.article_title: The 49-Point Gap: What SWE-bench Science's Visible-Test Scores Hide
claims.claim: Cursor's June 2026 audit found 63% of successful Claude Opus 4.8 Max resolutions on SWE-bench Pro were achieved by retrieval rather than derivation.

claims.article_title: The 49-Point Gap: What SWE-bench Science's Visible-Test Scores Hide
claims.claim: The non-empty input code in SWE-bench Science averages ~80,600 lines, and reference patches add ~118 lines on average.

claims.article_title: The 49-Point Gap: What SWE-bench Science's Visible-Test Scores Hide
claims.claim: SWE-Bench ProMax reports that a recent audit found nearly 60% of unsolved SWE-bench Verified instances contain flawed tests, and the best model achieves only 41.2% resolve rate on 170 refactoring tasks.

claims.article_title: The 49-Point Gap: What SWE-bench Science's Visible-Test Scores Hide
claims.claim: The same Claude-Opus-5 (max) configuration attains a 96.64% public score, producing a ~49-point visible-to-hidden gap.

claims.article_title: The 49-Point Gap: What SWE-bench Science's Visible-Test Scores Hide
claims.claim: The paper's conclusion states the gap 'shows that repository-level scientific software engineering requires scientific abstraction, disciplined exploration, system-wide integration, and generalization beyond visible cases.'

claims.article_title: The 49-Point Gap: What SWE-bench Science's Visible-Test Scores Hide
claims.claim: SWE-bench Science comprises 119 tasks from 98 GitHub repositories across 20 scientific domains.

claims.article_title: The 49-Point Gap: What SWE-bench Science's Visible-Test Scores Hide
claims.claim: SWE-bench Science organizes tasks into three paradigms: Issue-driven, Expert-exploratory, and Engineering-integration.

claims.article_title: The 49-Point Gap: What SWE-bench Science's Visible-Test Scores Hide
claims.claim: The benchmark's Chain-of-Evidence Protocol separates public and private tests, mounting private tests only after patch submission in a separate evaluator container.

claims.article_title: The 49-Point Gap: What SWE-bench Science's Visible-Test Scores Hide
claims.claim: PublicScore is the mean score across applicable public test cases, while Pass@1 is a binary exact-private-success measure equal to 1 only when every applicable private test passes.

claims.article_title: The 49-Point Gap: What SWE-bench Science's Visible-Test Scores Hide
claims.claim: DeepSeek-V4-Pro (max) scores 100.00% public and 42.02% overall Pass@1 on SWE-bench Science.

claims.article_title: The 49-Point Gap: What SWE-bench Science's Visible-Test Scores Hide
claims.claim: DeepSeek-V4-flash (high) scores 100.00% public and 19.33% overall Pass@1, and Qwen3.8-27B (max) scores 100.00% public and 29.41% overall Pass@1.

claims.article_title: The 49-Point Gap: What SWE-bench Science's Visible-Test Scores Hide
claims.claim: The paper identifies four recurring scientific failure mechanisms: scientific-knowledge/abstraction deficit, misguided exploration/surface-level repair, incomplete coverage/system integration, and scientific-knowledge generalization failure.

claims.article_title: The Jalapeño count: what an A0-stepping, unoptimized, Samsung-HBM4-bound ASIC actually settles against Vera Rubin
claims.claim: OpenAI released the first measured results for its Jalapeño inference ASIC on August 25, 2026, tested on SemiAnalysis's public InferenceX benchmark.

claims.article_title: The Jalapeño count: what an A0-stepping, unoptimized, Samsung-HBM4-bound ASIC actually settles against Vera Rubin
claims.claim: SemiAnalysis reports Jalapeño's HBM4 hits 10Gbps pin speeds giving 15.4TB/s bandwidth per package, a slight edge over the 9.6Gbps NVIDIA gets from HBM4 in Rubin, with the HBM 'likely provided by Samsung'.

claims.article_title: The Jalapeño count: what an A0-stepping, unoptimized, Samsung-HBM4-bound ASIC actually settles against Vera Rubin
claims.claim: On perf/TCO, SemiAnalysis reports Vera Rubin and Jalapeño are roughly head-to-head, producing almost the same number of output tokens per dollar, even though Rubin's results use speculative decoding while Jalapeño's do not.

claims.article_title: The Jalapeño count: what an A0-stepping, unoptimized, Samsung-HBM4-bound ASIC actually settles against Vera Rubin
claims.claim: OpenAI's blog disclosed that Codex working with GPT-Astra took three open-weight models not part of Jalapeño's original production plan to high performance within two months, and that AI-generated kernels beat expert-written kernels by 1.5-1.8x on selected GPT-OSS attention and MoE blocks.

claims.article_title: The Jalapeño count: what an A0-stepping, unoptimized, Samsung-HBM4-bound ASIC actually settles against Vera Rubin
claims.claim: OpenAI plans to begin deploying Jalapeño within its own compute infrastructure by the end of 2026, with hardware lead Richard Ho describing the initial volume as 'very small,' a gradual ramp over 2027, and most output at the end of next year.

claims.article_title: The Jalapeño count: what an A0-stepping, unoptimized, Samsung-HBM4-bound ASIC actually settles against Vera Rubin
claims.claim: The OpenAI-Broadcom partnership claims Jalapeño used a nine-month design-to-tapeout cycle and that OpenAI's own models accelerated parts of the chip design and optimization process.

claims.article_title: The Jalapeño count: what an A0-stepping, unoptimized, Samsung-HBM4-bound ASIC actually settles against Vera Rubin
claims.claim: SemiAnalysis suggests the CUDA moat may be eroding, noting OpenAI had no internal implementation of MLA kernels until benchmarking DeepSeek with InferenceX, and that Codex wrote efficient kernels without the kernel-engineering team intervening.

claims.article_title: The Jalapeño count: what an A0-stepping, unoptimized, Samsung-HBM4-bound ASIC actually settles against Vera Rubin
claims.claim: Compared against GB200/GB300 Blackwell systems on InferenceX, Jalapeño delivered 1.5-1.9x more AI work per watt at peak throughput and 1.7-3.6x lower end-to-end latency across GPT-OSS 120B, DeepSeek R1 670B, and Kimi K2.5 1T.

claims.article_title: The Jalapeño count: what an A0-stepping, unoptimized, Samsung-HBM4-bound ASIC actually settles against Vera Rubin
claims.claim: SemiAnalysis stated on August 25, 2026 that OpenAI's Jalapeño chip beats Vera Rubin's July results on Output Throughput per MW, i.e., it exceeds the Vera Rubin NVL72 figures NVIDIA and CoreWeave published in July.

claims.article_title: The Jalapeño count: what an A0-stepping, unoptimized, Samsung-HBM4-bound ASIC actually settles against Vera Rubin
claims.claim: The Jalapeño results were gathered on the A0 stepping of the chip, roughly nine months into the program with about three months of bring-up on actual silicon, and the comparison ran with single-token prediction, no MTP, no speculative decoding, no prefill/decode disaggregation, and pure tensor parallel.

claims.article_title: The Jalapeño count: what an A0-stepping, unoptimized, Samsung-HBM4-bound ASIC actually settles against Vera Rubin
claims.claim: Jalapeño is rated at 700W TDP while its measured sustained power remained at or below 550W on the tested workloads.

claims.article_title: The Jalapeño count: what an A0-stepping, unoptimized, Samsung-HBM4-bound ASIC actually settles against Vera Rubin
claims.claim: At matched prior-best time-between-tokens, Jalapeño delivers 54x to 104x the token throughput per kilowatt versus the best available accelerator, depending on model.

claims.article_title: The Jalapeño count: what an A0-stepping, unoptimized, Samsung-HBM4-bound ASIC actually settles against Vera Rubin
claims.claim: SemiAnalysis reports a B0 stepping of Jalapeño is already in the fab, delivering roughly a 25% perf-per-watt improvement over A0, with 13.4 PFLOPs of MXFP4 on a reticle-sized compute die on TSMC N3P.

claims.article_title: The Jalapeño count: what an A0-stepping, unoptimized, Samsung-HBM4-bound ASIC actually settles against Vera Rubin
claims.claim: Analyst Gavin Baker wrote that 'the real comparison will be with Rubin Ultra given Rubin shipping today,' with Feynman behind it, while also granting that OpenAI deserves 'credit where credit is due — first good ASIC outside of TPU/Trainium' and that Jalapeño submitted to a third-party benchmark before Google's TPUs ever did.

claims.article_title: The Jalapeño count: what an A0-stepping, unoptimized, Samsung-HBM4-bound ASIC actually settles against Vera Rubin
claims.claim: @jukan05 argued Jalapeño sources HBM4 almost exclusively from Samsung and therefore cannot scale to the same level as Rubin without relaxing its HBM4 speed requirement enough to qualify second sources.
